newsitem.title: ZAIRE: U.S. envoy hopes to salvage Zaire talks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy hopes to salvage Zaire talks.

text.p: U.S. envoy Bill Richardson said on Wednesday he hoped to salvage face-to-face talks between Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko and rebel leader Laurent Kabila.

"I am travelling to Kinshasa later today and I have a lot to talk to Mr Mobutu about," said Richardson, the U.S. ambassador to the United Nations, shortly after arriving in the northeast Zairean capital Kisangani.
Richardson, who arrived in Kisangani to see the plight of thousands of Rwandan Hutu refugees in eastern Zaire, said he was still optimistic that talks between Kabila and Mobutu could take place.
"I must be," he said. "We still have a possibility of other venues, even this venue...we will just have to wait and see."
Zairean rebels on Wednesday shrugged off Mobutu's refusal to meet Kabila aboard a South African navy ship and said they would push on towards the capital Kinshasa.
Richardson on Wednesday visited a camp for refugees awaiting a U.N. airlift to take them home to Rwanda.
